newsitem.title: CANADA: Minister says APEC sees smooth Hong Kong transfer.
newsitem.headline: Minister says APEC sees smooth Hong Kong transfer.

text.p: Asia-Pacific trade ministers expect a smooth transition from British to Chinese rule for Hong Kong, Hong Kong's Secretary of Trade and Industry Chung-yee Denise Yue said.

In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, broadcast on Monday morning, Yue said Asia Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) trade ministers did not expect Hong Kong's open-market business environment to change after the handover on July 1.
"Trade and economics are the two areas, amongst others, where Hong Kong will continue to enjoy a very high degree of autonomy after the transition," she said.
Yue made the comments on Friday during a three-day meeting of APEC trade ministers hosted by Canada.
In the interview, Yue said she did not think that Shanghai would displace Hong Kong as the stock market and financial hub for the Southeast Asian region after July 1.
"I would be very surprised if that were the case because there are fundamental differences between Hong Kong and Shanghai," Yue said.
"Shanghai will be a market operating in a socialist economy, whereas the Hong Kong stock market will operate within the capitalist economy," she said.

Yue said regulations and legal frameworks were very different between Shanghai and Hong Kong, and that China's Renminbi was not a full convertible currency, while the Hong Kong dollar would remain a convertible currency pegged to the U.S. dollar.
